subject: Biology
topic: Human heart and circulation — mixed tiers
description: Chambers, valves, ECG, blood pressure, cardiac cycle, common pathologies

questions.stem: The human heart has how many chambers?
questions.explanation: Four chambers: right atrium → right ventricle → pulmonary artery → lungs (deoxygenated blood); left atrium ← pulmonary veins ← lungs (oxygenated blood) → left ventricle → aorta. Septum between left and right halves prevents mixing. Average size ~fist, mass ~300 g, beats ~72 bpm at rest = ~100,000 beats/day. Fish — 2 chambers (1A + 1V); frogs/reptiles — 3 (2A + 1V, except crocodiles); birds + mammals — 4 (complete double circulation).

questions.stem: The valve between the LEFT atrium and LEFT ventricle of the human heart is called the:
questions.explanation: Four heart valves: TRICUSPID (right atrium ↔ right ventricle, 3 cusps); BICUSPID / MITRAL (left atrium ↔ left ventricle, 2 cusps; named after a 'mitre' — bishop's headgear); PULMONARY semilunar (RV ↔ pulmonary artery); AORTIC semilunar (LV ↔ aorta). Mnemonic 'LAB RAT' — Left = Atrium-Bicuspid, Right = Atrium-Tricuspid. 'Lub-dub' heart sounds: Lub = AV valves close (tricuspid + mitral); Dub = semilunar valves close.

questions.stem: The natural pacemaker of the heart, which initiates each heartbeat, is the:

options.option_text: SA node (sino-atrial node) in the right atrium

questions.explanation: Conduction pathway — SA node (sinoatrial, in right atrial wall, ~100 bpm intrinsic rate, slowed to ~72 by vagal tone) → atrial muscle → AV node (atrioventricular, brief delay ~0.1s lets atria fully empty) → Bundle of His → Right + Left bundle branches → Purkinje fibres → ventricular muscle. Each firing produces an ECG wave (P = atrial depolarisation, QRS = ventricular depolarisation, T = ventricular repolarisation).

questions.stem: Normal blood pressure for a healthy adult at rest is approximately:
questions.explanation: Systolic / Diastolic = 120 / 80 mmHg ideally. Systolic — peak pressure when ventricles contract; diastolic — minimum when ventricles relax. Hypertension: ≥140/90 (Stage 1); Pre-hypertension 120-139 / 80-89; Hypotension <90/60. Measured with sphygmomanometer (Korotkoff sounds via stethoscope) or digital. Risk factors — smoking, salt, stress, obesity, alcohol, family history. Untreated hypertension → stroke, heart failure, kidney disease.

questions.stem: The 'pulmonary' circulation refers to blood flow between the:
questions.explanation: Two circulations: PULMONARY (heart → lungs → heart, oxygenates blood); SYSTEMIC (heart → body → heart, delivers oxygen to tissues). Pulmonary artery — only artery carrying DEOXYGENATED blood (RV → lungs). Pulmonary veins — only veins carrying OXYGENATED blood (lungs → LA). Discovered fully by William Harvey in 1628 (De Motu Cordis). Pulmonary circulation operates at much LOWER pressure (~25/8 mmHg) than systemic — reason for the thin-walled pulmonary artery vs muscular aorta.

questions.stem: The chamber of the heart with the THICKEST muscular wall is the:

options.option_text: Left ventricle (must pump blood to entire body via aorta)

questions.explanation: Left ventricle wall is ~3-4× thicker than right ventricle's because it generates the systemic blood pressure (~120 mmHg) — pumping blood through the aorta to every body tissue. Right ventricle has lower pressure (~25 mmHg pulmonary) — needs less muscle. Atria are thin-walled — they only push blood ~5 mmHg into the next-door ventricle. Hypertension causes Left Ventricular Hypertrophy (LVH) — thicker wall but stiffer = poorer filling.

questions.stem: Blood components by volume — plasma is roughly:

options.option_text: 55% of blood; the rest 45% is cells (mostly RBCs)

questions.explanation: Whole blood: plasma ~55% (water 90%, proteins 7%, ions, glucose, etc.) + cellular ('formed elements') ~45% — RBCs (4.5-5.5 million/µL, dominate by volume), WBCs (4-11 thousand/µL — 5 types: neutrophil, lymphocyte, monocyte, eosinophil, basophil), platelets (1.5-4 lakh/µL). Hematocrit (PCV) = % cells = ~40-50% in adults. Plasma without clotting factors = serum (used in medical tests). Total adult blood volume ~5-5.5 litres.
